subtype: Approach: seeking a trusted friend's view [Action]
passage: At a café table in Addis Ababa, Abebe turned a laptop toward Clara, a friend. A reviewer on a travel forum had called Abebe's guesthouse 'dirty, with rude staff', and Abebe had written a reply overnight. 'Read it as if you don't know me,' Abebe said. Clara, who had never stayed there and had nothing riding on it, read slowly. 'The third line is sarcastic: "Sorry our standards weren't luxury enough for you." Take it out. And you never say what you'll do.' Abebe winced, then nodded. Together they cut the sarcasm and added a promise: 'We've changed the cleaning checklist, and I'll message you directly.' Abebe read it once more, said, 'That sounds like me on a good day,' and posted it before lunch.

qa.q: Which line did Clara say to take out?
qa.a: Clara said to take out the sarcastic third line, 'Sorry our standards weren't luxury enough for you.'

qa.q: How did Abebe feel about Clara's comment on the sarcasm, and what shows it?
qa.a: Abebe winced and then nodded, stung at first but ready to accept it.

qa.q: What could Abebe have done if no friend was free to read the draft?
qa.a: Abebe could have waited a day before posting, since overnight anger fades and a calmer reading shows the sarcasm.

qa.q: How might the reviewer see the final reply?
qa.a: The reviewer would probably feel heard, since the reply promised a change and a direct message and did not mock. 🙂

grounding: Shows a person sharing a draft reply with a friend who is not emotionally involved, who suggests removing sarcasm and adding a concrete promise.

passage:
In the corner of the coworking space's café, Rekha turned her laptop toward Rafiq. 'Read this before I post it. The complaint is from a school that says our booking software double-booked their hall.'
Rafiq read it slowly. Her draft began: 'Perhaps if your staff read our help page, this wouldn't happen.' It ended with, 'We'll look into it.'
'Honest opinion?' he said. 'The first line is sarcasm. They'll screenshot it. And "we'll look into it" means nothing.'
'But it was partly their mistake.'
'Maybe. Say that privately. In public, say what you'll actually do.'
Rekha deleted the first line. In its place: 'We're sorry for the trouble this caused your event.' She changed the ending to: 'We'll call your office today and add a double-booking warning by next Monday.' Rafiq nodded. She posted it.

qa.q: What did Rekha's draft begin with?
qa.a: 'Perhaps if your staff read our help page, this wouldn't happen.'

qa.q: What was Rekha feeling when she wrote the first draft?
qa.a: She was defensive and irritated, feeling the school was partly to blame.
Rafiq wasn't emotionally involved, so he could see the sarcasm and the empty promise that Rekha missed.

qa.q: How might the school see the posted reply?
qa.a: The school gets an apology and a concrete promise, a call today and a warning by Monday, so it feels taken seriously.

grounding: It shows someone sharing a draft reply with an uninvolved friend who suggests removing sarcasm and adding a concrete promise.

passage:
Hi Vandana,
Thank you for reading my reply draft at eleven last night. I wanted to tell you what happened.
You were right about the line 'Some customers clearly didn't read the instructions.' I'd thought it was clever. You said it would be the only line anyone remembered. I cut it.
You also said my promise, 'We're working on improvements', was too vague. So I wrote what we're actually doing: 'The new setup guide goes live this Friday, and we'll reply to every open ticket by Wednesday.'
I posted it at nine this morning. By noon, the person who had complained replied, 'Thank you, that's all I wanted.' Two others said the same.
If I'd posted my version, I think I'd be in a fight right now. Next time I'm sending you the draft before I even show my co-founder.
Nilesh

qa.q: When will the new setup guide go live?
How does Nilesh feel after the replies at noon?
qa.a: Nilesh feels relieved and grateful, sure that the original draft would have started a fight.

qa.q: What else could Nilesh do to make this a habit?
qa.a: Nilesh could wait a few hours before posting any reply and always ask one calm person to read it first.

qa.q: How might Vandana feel reading the thank-you email?
qa.a: Vandana would likely feel valued and pleased that the honest suggestions made a real difference.

grounding: It shows someone sharing a draft response with a friend not emotionally involved, who suggests removing sarcasm and adding a concrete promise.
